items.title: News Podcast: Indie Manga Alliance Launches, Libro.fm Adds E-books, and Readers Fail to Spot AI Stories
items.excerpt: A new US-based Indie Manga Alliance launches to represent independent manga creators as AI production tools spread through comics, alongside Libro.fm's move into e-books. The episode also unpacks a Cambridge University Press study showing readers cannot reliably tell AI-written stories from human ones.

items.title: 10k sign petition demanding legislation on AI firms to disclose training data
items.excerpt: A petition backed by authors and publishers has passed 10,000 signatures, calling for a statutory requirement that AI companies disclose the copyrighted works in their training data. It escalates the UK trade's push for transparency-first AI regulation.
items.note: Date exact from article page (2026-08-13); clock time approximated to 09:00Z (site blocks our UA for meta extraction).

items.title: Commonwealth Foundation to delay Short Story Prize submissions after AI controversy
items.excerpt: The Commonwealth Foundation is postponing 2027 Short Story Prize entries and reviewing its processes after allegations that AI was used in the 2026 competition. Literary prizes are being forced to rewrite submission rules around generative tools.
items.note: Date exact from article page (2026-08-12); clock time approximated to 09:00Z.

items.title: Authors need transparent AI policies, if only to protect themselves
items.excerpt: Novelist Jamie Fewery argues that writers should publish an explicit personal AI policy — what they use, what they refuse — as basic professional self-defence in a market now primed to accuse. A practical craft-and-disclosure playbook rather than a manifesto.
items.note: Date exact from article page (2026-08-12); clock time approximated to 09:00Z.

items.title: Claude is adding watermarks to generated content
items.excerpt: Anthropic will embed watermarks and digitally signed provenance metadata in Claude's output to meet EU transparency law. For writers and editors it means AI-assisted drafts may now carry machine-readable traces into the manuscript pipeline.

items.title: Five Pulitzer winners disclosed AI use this year
items.excerpt: Five winners across 15 journalism categories disclosed AI use in their entries, the most since disclosure began in 2024, and next year's book submissions will add an AI disclosure question. Award-level disclosure is becoming a norm writers have to plan for.

items.title: ChatGPT blocks requests to imitate specific writers' styles
items.excerpt: OpenAI now refuses prompts asking ChatGPT to write in the style of a named author. Style isn't protected by copyright, but the guardrail reshapes a very common author workflow — and signals how litigation pressure is editing the tools themselves.

items.title: Spammers and Scammers: What to Do When Your Book Is Sold Under a False Name
items.excerpt: ALLi's scam-watch series walks through the identity-hijack economy now supercharged by cheap generative output: fake author names, cloned titles and AI-padded listings sold on major retailers. Includes the takedown steps indie authors can actually run.

items.title: News Podcast: Literary Agents Update Ethics Rules; Seven-Figure Deal Shelved Over AI Claims; Study Examines AI Books on Amazon
items.excerpt: The Association of American Literary Agents rewrites its ethics guidance while a seven-figure novel deal collapses over AI allegations. Dan Holloway ties both to the peer-reviewed study of 14,000+ self-published Amazon titles.

items.title: The Published Voice: Whose Voice Are We Really Reading?
items.excerpt: Roohi Ghosh asks what 'author voice' still means once AI editing sits between draft and published text. A craft-level argument about how much smoothing a manuscript can absorb before the writer disappears from it.

items.title: Digital Science Launches AI-native Researcher Workspace
items.excerpt: Digital Science released Papers AI, an AI-native writing and reading workspace built by the Overleaf team, where researchers draft, take notes and query sources in one place. Every AI-suggested edit requires explicit user acceptance — a design stance worth noting.

items.title: Around the Book World: August 10, 2026
items.excerpt: News Corp's Robert Thomson says 'AI can really transform audiobooks' with far more voice choice and sound design, while HarperCollins turns AI on overseas translation. The roundup also logs a record five Pulitzer winners disclosing AI use.

items.title: Brian Murray Addresses AI Authorship Issues
items.excerpt: HarperCollins CEO Brian Murray calls for industry-wide standards on AI authorship after a run of cancelled book deals over suspected AI use. He wants shared disclosure norms rather than ad-hoc accusations title by title.
items.note: PW exposes no og/JSON-LD publish time; date exact from byline block (08/06/2026 @ 11:00AM ET), stored as 15:00Z.

items.title: New BISG Head Lays Out Priorities
items.excerpt: New BISG executive director Allison Belan says 'AI was the first thing that came up in virtually every conversation' with members, and wants the standards body to move from theory to practical implementation guidance. Metadata, identifiers and AI disclosure top the list.
items.note: PW date exact from byline block (08/07/2026); clock time stored as 15:00Z.

items.title: Princeton University Press Partners with Cashmere on AI Licensing
items.excerpt: Princeton University Press will make its catalog available to 'copyright compliant' AI platforms through licensing startup Cashmere, keeping title-by-title control over what gets licensed. An opt-in template other presses are watching.
items.note: PW date exact from byline block (08/03/2026); clock time stored as 15:00Z.

items.title: Anthropic says it will watermark text generated by its AI models
items.excerpt: Anthropic will watermark text produced by Claude to comply with EU rules that took effect in early August, and says the marks survive copy-paste across platforms. The tooling-side detail behind publishing's new AI-disclosure fights.

items.title: HarperCollins is betting big on AI Audiobooks
items.excerpt: HarperCollins is scaling ElevenLabs-powered synthetic narration across backlist and foreign-language titles while insisting human narration stays its core product. Voice actors read the split differently.
items.note: Date exact from article page (2026-08-07); clock time approximated to 12:00Z (site returns 403 to our UA for feed/meta). Overlaps the HarperCollins AI-audiobook thread flagged in recent_coverage_skipped — included only for outlet diversity, deprioritize.
